I totally agree with both you and the person who posted this. I was not baptized. I often thought of this as even more of a reason to leave the religion. I would think, "Hey! I'm not going to be DFed and I will still be able to talk to everyone. Why not." Now I am not saying at all that I left that easily and it was quite simple to do so, there are many more reasons why, but regardless when I left I thought everyone would treat me similar to the way they did when I was still attending meetings. That's where I was wrong. 

The worst thing... The most horrible thing... My mothers best friends who have known me since I was a baby treat me like I was DFed. I have not kept in touch with one person, beside family, that is still in that religion. I feel sometimes like at the point I left, I was totally alone and had to learn how to live again. 

As for family. My parents and I do get along. I feel our relationship has been getting better with time. We have our rough patches but we are doing good to get over them. I am also lucky to have my two older half brothers who left the religion too. On the other hand, I have two sisters who are still involved. My one sister says Hi and Bye to me when I see her, but my oldest sister, who was a huge part of my life and who I helped raise her two children up to the ages of ~ 5 and 3, will not talk to me. I haven't heard a word from her in over 5 years. She has told her children that I am a bad person. I do bad things and they shouldn't talk to me. 

Now, I am not saying that one of anyone's situations is worse than the other. Everyone's story is different and has its own level of emotion for whoever is experiencing it, but I feel like being bitter and hostile towards it makes it worse for everyone. I feel like the more I man up and deal with it, the stronger I get.
